semester )\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EAge : 19 years\u003Cbr\u003E\nSex : Male\u003Cbr\u003E\nOccupation : College student\u003Cbr\u003E\nState : West Bengal\u003Cbr\u003E\nYear : 2017\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#Chief complains\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E1. Recurrent fever\u003Cbr\u003E\n2. Pain around left iliac crest\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#History of present illness\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003ESince 3 months, the patient is\u0026nbsp;suffering from recurrent fever. When he started taking medicine the fever subsided. But as he stopped taking the medicines​ , he again\u0026nbsp;developed fever. There is no particular timing of his fever. He has developed hepatomegaly and along with\u0026nbsp; sign of pallor. It seems that he also has pleural effusion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EAnd , due to arthralgia , he was unable to extend at the level of his Right elbow.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#History of past illness\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003ERegarding the Pain\u003Cbr\u003E\n1. Onset \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; : 20 - 25 days ago,\u0026nbsp; for 4 - 5 days ,then followed by fever\u003Cbr\u003E\n2. Position \u0026nbsp; : Pain around left iliac crest\u003Cbr\u003E\n3. Quality \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; : continous pain\u003Cbr\u003E\n4. Relieving or Aggravating factor : no such factor\u003Cbr\u003E\n5. Severity \u0026nbsp; : intolerable\u003Cbr\u003E\n6. Timing \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; : no specific timing\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EHe never had any major or minor surgery operated on him.\u003Cbr\u003E\nAlso , 2.5 months ago , he was diagnosed with Typhoid fever.\u003Cbr\u003E\nThen after medication, he was apparently well for the next 15 days. He suddenly developed malaise followed by a series of recurrent fever.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003ESubcutaneous spot of bleeding could be seen in left arm.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EA supernumerary nipple can also be seen on the left half of abdomen along the milk line (Line of Schultz).\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#Family history\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EGrandmother - breast cancer\u003Cbr\u003E\nAunt - died undiagnosed\u003Cbr\u003E\nFather - died at the age of 28 years,\u0026nbsp; due to rectal cancer\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#Drug history\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\nNo allergy for drugs.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#Personal history\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EAppetite\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp; : normal\u003Cbr\u003E\nSleep\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp; : normal\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\nBuilt \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;: weak and slim\u003Cbr\u003E\nRate of respiration \u0026nbsp; : High (\u0026gt; 30 breaths per minute)\u003Cbr\u003E\nPulse rate \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;: High (95 pulses per minute)\u003Cbr\u003E\nHeart rate \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;: High ( tachycardia)\u003Cbr\u003E\nTremors, Cyanosis, Clubbing \u0026nbsp;: absent\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#Findings\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EUSG report of whole abdomen shows that liver is enlarged in size, gallbladder is contracted, spleen is normal in size with echotexture.\u003Cbr\u003E\nMild free fluid is also seen in the peritoneal​ cavity.\u003Cbr\u003E\nThus, hepatomegaly and mild Ascites has been inferred.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#Peripheral Smear Findings\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003ERBC : RBCs predominantly Normocytic Normochromic. Moderate anisopoikiliocytosis seen. Moderate polychromasia seen , nRBCs - 17\/100\u003Cbr\u003E\nWBC : Total count within normal limits . Blasts - 40 % , Neutrophil - 26 % , Lymphocytes - 28 % , Eosinophils - 1% ,Monocytes - 5%\u003Cbr\u003E\nPlatelet : Reduced on smear\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EFinally , when immunophenotyping was performed it has been observed that it's a case of precursor B cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia ( Pre\u0026nbsp;B-ALL) with a aberrant CD33 expression.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E#And now , here are few University questions, related to the topic , that are often asked :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EPathology\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E1. text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003E#Treatment of the patient\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EAt present patient is in remission ( disease free) after first induction therapy. But MRD positive means minimal residual disease present. He is taking second phase of chemotherapy in day care.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003E#Method in use : The Berlin-Frankfurt-Munster (BFM) 2002 ALL Protocols\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003E#Details of the treatment method\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EAcute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in Children\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EA Brief Review of the Internationally Available Protocols\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EThe following medicines are available in the first edition of the Essential Medicines List for children.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ECytotoxic medicines\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EComplementary \u0026nbsp;List \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EA) allopurinol \u0026nbsp; Tablet: \u0026nbsp;100 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;to \u0026nbsp;300 \u0026nbsp;mg. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EB) asparaginase \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;10 \u0026nbsp;000 \u0026nbsp;IU \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EC) bleomycin \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;15 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(as \u0026nbsp;sulfate) \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ED) calcium \u0026nbsp;folinate \u0026nbsp; Injection: \u0026nbsp;3 \u0026nbsp;mg\/ml \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;10‐ml \u0026nbsp;ampoule. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ETablet: \u0026nbsp;15 \u0026nbsp;mg. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EE) chlorambucil \u0026nbsp; Tablet: \u0026nbsp;2 \u0026nbsp;mg. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EF)cisplatin \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;10 \u0026nbsp;mg; \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EG) cyclophosphamide Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;500 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ETablet: \u0026nbsp;25 \u0026nbsp;mg. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EH) cytarabine \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;100 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EI) dacarbazine \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;100 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EJ) dactinomycin \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;500 \u0026nbsp;micrograms \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EK) daunorubicin \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(as \u0026nbsp;hydrochloride). \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EL) doxorubicin \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;10 \u0026nbsp;mg; \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(hydrochloride)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003Ein \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EM) etoposide \u0026nbsp; Capsule: \u0026nbsp;100 \u0026nbsp;mg. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EInjection: \u0026nbsp;20 \u0026nbsp;mg\/ml \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;5‐ml \u0026nbsp;ampoule. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EN) fluorouracil \u0026nbsp; Injection: \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg\/ml \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;5‐ml \u0026nbsp;ampoule. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EO) mercaptopurine \u0026nbsp; Tablet: \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EP) methotrexate \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(as \u0026nbsp;sodium \u0026nbsp;salt) \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ETablet: \u0026nbsp;2.5 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(as \u0026nbsp;sodium \u0026nbsp;salt). \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EQ) procarbazine \u0026nbsp; Capsule: \u0026nbsp;50 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(as \u0026nbsp;hydrochloride). \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ER) vinblastine \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;10 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(sulfate) \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003ES) vincristine \u0026nbsp; Powder \u0026nbsp;for \u0026nbsp;injection: \u0026nbsp;1 \u0026nbsp;mg; \u0026nbsp;5 \u0026nbsp;mg \u0026nbsp;(sulfate) \u0026nbsp;in \u0026nbsp;vial.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; text-align: start;\"\u003EUnder the BFM 2002 ALL Protocols\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: start;\"\u003E\u003Cfont face=\"sans-serif\"\u003EOutline of Induction has been given below in the diagram\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: start;\"\u003E\u003Cfont face=\"sans-serif\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: start;\"\u003E\u003Cfont face=\"sans-serif\"\u003Eand one dose of methotrexate (MTX) intrathecally (IT) on day 1. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif; 1st year MBBS experience "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EAfter clearing my Medical entrance, I got admission in a medical school . Joining medical school was like dream come true. I was really happy and excited about a completely new experience. I feel proud to be a part of this medical community , as I can now actually do something directly for the people of my country.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EEvery year lakhs of science stream students prepare for Medical entrance,\u0026#160; but only a handful of them cross the exam. Things are getting harder day by day due to increased competition and quality of education. Internet has made things easier, and knowledge available for everyone anytime. \u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EI still remember, when I was in 1st year MBBS. It was really difficult for to me cope with the new syllabus. For the first 2 months , i couldn't understand what to do and what not to. \u003Cbr\u003E\nIn reality I didn't know how to study. \u003Cbr\u003E\nIn the beginning I used to fail in most of the PCT ( part completion test ). I could not even secure 50% mark in these exams. It was really confusing as I had no idea\u0026#160; , what the professor is going to ask and which topic is more important. And finally after some time I somehow managed to adjust myself with the situation. Whatever be the situation just say yourself\u0026#160;\u0026#8220; I will never give up \u0026#8221; . I decided to make plans before implementation of any idea. In the beginning all my plans failed , be it Plan A or Plan Y. After , soon I started improving. Soon results came in my favour. I started learning from my mistakes. Each time i was becoming better and more powerful than earlier. i started making better , more improved and smart Plans.\u003Cbr\u003E\nWell said by Dr. Vishram Singh \u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E\u0026#8220;To learn from previous experience and change accordingly, makes you a successful man.\u0026#8221;\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EFinally , my 1st year mbbs professional exam approached. I didn't panic this time, instead i gave my exam with confidence , without thinking much about negative consequences.\u003Cbr\u003E\nAfter 1 month , it was the time for declaration of exam's result. I was out of control , i didn't know how to control my mind and emotions. \u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EFinally , at 7:30 pm , i got to know that our result has been declared. I was severely shivering. One of my friend asked me for my Roll number; this time i was out of this world. I , then gave my Roll number to him and asked to check the result. But , one more disaster was waiting for me , NO Internet Connection. I could feel my heartbeat and all signs of Tachycardia. After 5 minutes I got internet connection, and the page reloaded. I saw in the next page : PASS .\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EWhat a relief,\u0026#160; this word was the Word of the Day in my Dictionary for that day. I passed all the subjects , with better marks than I expected . I discovered , Physiology as the strongest subject with more marks , than other subjects .I was still shivering and full of adrenaline rush. I could not understand,\u0026#160; how to celebrate my success , shall I Dance , Jump from a tower or shall I take a mike and announce everywhere about this news. \u003Cbr\u003E\nNow , I was gonna be a Senior. I will be in 2nd year MBBS. New subjects,\u0026#160; New experience and One more challenge. \u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EAt the end , I just wanna say one thing !\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003E\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160; \u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160;\u0026#160; \u0026#8220; A Goal Without A Plan, Is Just A Wish \u0026#8221;.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003EThis was my experience of 1st year in my medical school. You can also share your feelings in the comment section below. I will happy to listen your reactions about the article. \u003Cbr\u003E\nThanks everyone for viewing my page .\u003C\/p\u003E\n"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/santusaha235.blogspot.com\/feeds\/3384015507809227684\/comments\/default","title":"Post Comments"},{"rel":"replies","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/santusaha235.blogspot.com\/2016\/12\/my-1st-year-mbbs-experience.html#comment-form","title":"0 Comments"},{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/7868470865885078060\/posts\/default\/3384015507809227684"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/7868470865885078060\/posts\/default\/3384015507809227684"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/santusaha235.blogspot.com\/2016\/12\/my-1st-year-mbbs-experience.html","title":"My 1st year MBBS experience "}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"Santu Saha"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/17809879165967604862"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"19","height":"32","src":"\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEiv8sZVpO1W9JXmS1OqhRUkBLzuIjehi1mhzR0GELl83_tAuxqy_ZoZ5ihbmudovMm9yMYDkn4_rQEUILmsum3w4UONf2xIilC6w2sU100DKE4Tv2Gfxt3zu7qFvJcYess\/s113\/Wiki_med_logo_no_outline.svg.png"}}],"thr$total":{"$t":"0"}}]}}
